problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by 

$$
s(t)={t}^{2}-2t+\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity at time $t=3.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2t+\operatorname{ln}⁡t) \\  & =2t-2+\frac{1}{t}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the velocity at $t=3,$ we substitute $t=3$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =2(3)-2+\frac{1}{3} \\  & =6-2+\frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{13}{3} \\  & =4.333\,333… \\  & ≈4.33\end{aligned}
$$
